audit.whatIsWrong: The entire full layer tracks an ability called 'Repeating Dashes' — it appears in tldr, winCon, enemyWin, loading, focus.text, four breakdown keys, three phases, dosFull and six report sections. Ambessa has no ability by that name.
audit.why: Her kit is Drakehound's Step (P), Cunning Sweep / Sundering Slam (Q), Repudiation (W), Lacerate (E), Public Execution (R). 'Repeating Dashes' is a descriptive placeholder that got frozen into the data as if it were a Riot name, so every 'track X' instruction in this matchup points at a button the player cannot find. I have standardised on Lacerate, her E, because the entry's own focus.letters already reads ['E'] and Lacerate is the dash with a real trackable cooldown (13/12/11/10/9); Drakehound's Step has no cooldown of its own since it fires off any ability cast.
audit.corrected: Lacerate (E), 13/12/11/10/9 — the trackable dash. Drakehound's Step (P) is the free dash off any ability cast and cannot be tracked on a timer.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json — P Drakehound's Step, Q Cunning Sweep/Sundering Slam, W Repudiation, E Lacerate (13/12/11/10/9), R Public Execution

audit.whatIsWrong: Repudiation is never mentioned, and four strings vaguely attribute her extended-trade damage to 'W damage' / 'her W melee damage' without saying what W does.
audit.why: This is the single most exploitable interaction in the matchup and it is currently inverted. Repudiation shields Ambessa, braces, then slams — and if she blocked any NON-MINION damage during the brace, the slam deals INCREASED damage. A Teemo whose instinct is to keep auto-attacking and stacking poison is actively feeding the ability. The correct play is to stop attacking for the brace and resume the instant it pops. Nothing in the entry tells the player this; the current text encourages the opposite.
audit.corrected: Repudiation (W), 18/17/16/15/14: shield + brace + slam. Damage blocked during the brace empowers the slam. Hold your autos and poison through the brace.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json — W Repudiation: 'gains a shield, briefly braces herself, and then slams the ground... If she blocked any non-minion damage while bracing herself, this ability will deal increased damage.'

audit.whatIsWrong: Public Execution is never named or described anywhere in either layer, despite being her kill button.
audit.why: It blinks her to the FARTHEST enemy champion in a line she chooses, then suppresses and stuns. The counterintuitive consequence for a squishy Teemo is that standing behind a teammate does not shield you — being furthest down the line is precisely what selects you. Positioning to the side of the likely line, rather than behind an ally, is the answer, and it is nowhere in the entry.
audit.corrected: Public Execution (R), 1250 range, 130/115/100s: blinks to the FARTHEST champion in the chosen line. Hiding behind an ally makes you the target.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json — R Public Execution: 'blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line of her choosing and suppresses them upon her arrival', range 1250, cooldown 130/115/100

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] states 'Your Q is now max-rank at level 3'.
audit.why: At champion level 3 Teemo has three ability points total, so Q cannot be above rank 2 — max rank is impossible before level 9. The conclusion the line draws is fine, but it is hung on an impossible premise, and the real reason is better anyway: Blinding Dart is 7 seconds flat from rank 1, so the pre-emptive blind is already available on that cadence at level 3 without any rank investment.
audit.corrected: Blinding Dart is 7s flat at rank 1 — the pre-emptive blind cadence exists from level 1, no max rank required.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json — Q cooldown '7' (single value, all ranks)

audit.whatIsWrong: Drakehound's Step is described only as 'passive-loaded dash chain' with no mention of what it grants.
audit.why: It grants her next ATTACK bonus range, damage and attack speed. That empowered hit is a basic attack, which means Blinding Dart deletes it — the specific thing a Teemo should be spending his blind on. The entry currently tells the player to blind 'as she commits her dash chain', which is close but never names the payload that makes the blind worth it.
audit.corrected: Drakehound's Step dashes off any ability cast and empowers her next basic attack — blind that attack.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json — P: 'granting her next attack bonus range, damage, and attack speed, and refunding energy'

edits.before: At level 1 you are not guaranteed dominance here — Ambessa's passive-loaded dash can close before your Blinding Shot resolves, and her damage in that first burst window is legitimate. Keep max range with Toxic Shot, auto her once and back, never stand still in the open. If she steps forward to CS, a Q preemptively thrown forces her to either eat the blind on her next dash-weave or back off — but do not throw it reactively after she has already dashed, it will miss. Your actual poke pattern at 1-2 is E auto, micro-back with W, repeat; you are winning by attrition not by brawling.
edits.after: At level 1 you are not guaranteed dominance — Drakehound's Step dashes her off any ability cast, so she closes before your Blinding Dart resolves, and that first burst is legitimate. Keep max range with Toxic Shot, auto her once and back, never stand still in the open. If she steps up to CS, a pre-emptive Q forces her to either eat the blind on her empowered attack or back off; thrown reactively after the dash it just misses. Never auto into her Repudiation brace — non-minion damage she blocks there makes the slam hit harder. Your pattern at 1-2 is E auto, micro-back with W, repeat: attrition, not brawling.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 belong to Ambessa — her dash chains let her follow your W burst speed and the W melee damage in that window is high enough to punish any extended trade. Shroom the tribush now and keep the river entrance warded so you see her coming and can pre-activate W before she reaches you. Your mushrooms slow her mid-chase, buying the half-second you need to escape. At level 6 the dynamic shifts: Noxious Trap gives you an escape lattice she cannot safely dash through — she will hit a shroom during any chase, lose MS, and eat another poison stack, which with a Liandry's start in progress becomes real damage.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 belong to Ambessa — her dash chains follow your W burst speed and her Q chain plus Lacerate's slow punish any extended trade. Shroom the tribush now and keep the river entrance warded so you see her coming and can pre-activate W. Never auto into Repudiation's brace: damage she blocks there empowers the slam, so hold poke until it pops, then resume. At level 6 the dynamic shifts — Noxious Trap gives you an escape lattice she cannot safely dash through: she hits a shroom during any chase, loses MS, and eats another poison stack, which with Liandry's in progress becomes real damage.

edits.before: Liandry's Angueur changes the math: Toxic Shot into poison stacks into Liandry's burn means every trade she starts costs her a chunk of HP even if she dashes out immediately. Place mushrooms on every common re-engage angle around the lane — she cannot freely dash through brush she cannot see. Your win condition is a shroom-warded side lane where every path to you is mined, forcing her to spend time clearing vision or eating 40% HP in mushroom damage on the way in. In a straight side-by-side duel she can still win, so never let her close without a Q blind landing first — the combo of blind plus poison plus mushroom slow is the only sequence where you reliably come out ahead.

notes: The flagged suspect name 'Lay Noxious Trap' in wants.you[2] is a FALSE POSITIVE — Noxious Trap is correct and the detector tripped on the leading verb. The genuine naming problem is far larger and is in the FULL layer, not the content layer: 'Repeating Dashes' is not an Ambessa ability at all, and it appears roughly sixteen times. I replaced it with Lacerate (E) in the fifteen highest-visibility strings, chosen to match the entry's existing focus.letters ['E'].
